title: Grapheme clusters follow UAX #29 extended grapheme clusters
cm6: @marijn/find-cluster-break 1.0.4 joins a code point of its table (Unicode 17.0 Extend and SpacingMark below U+30000), anything next to a ZWJ, and regional-indicator pairs (mirrors/marijn/find-cluster-break/src/index.js:45-66). So a Hangul syllable written as jamo splits into its letters, an Indic conjunct breaks after the virama, a Prepend character stands alone, tag sequences (the flag of England) and variation selectors at or above U+E0100 (ideographic variants) split from their base, CR LF inside a string is two clusters, a control takes a following mark, and a ZWJ joins whatever follows it. The 181 fixtures of state.findClusterBreak.B9 record these.
better: The cursor, deletion, columns and word lookup never stop inside what the person editing sees as one character: the extended grapheme clusters of UAX #29 (rules GB3 to GB9c, GB11 to GB13), at the Unicode version of cm6's table or later, so that no character cm6 groups is split.
basis: Unicode Standard Annex #29, the rule native text systems and the shapers of the surfaces use (the harness's Node gives it through Intl.Segmenter, ICU 78.3, Unicode 17.0, and docs/parity/ferrum-state/oracle/cm6/text/s4-fix5.ts recorded where it differs from cm6). cm6's reason is its stack: a small table shipped in a JavaScript bundle; its README promises only extending characters, ZWJ and flags.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch that replaces findClusterBreak in the harness by one built on Intl.Segmenter; GraphemeBreakTest.txt of the same Unicode version against the patched cm6 and against Ferrum.
note: To gather before it is made (rust-researcher): the Unicode version of the Rust implementation against 17.0 (a crate, or tables generated from the UCD: a library choice of D2); what `include_extending == false` means under the full rule (cm6 uses it for backspace, commands.ts:581-585, where it removes one mark, and today also one jamo); whether any sequence cm6 groups would split (ZWJ before a non-pictograph), which the floor forbids. Risk: low once the floor is shown; one function and one table change. Adopting it at design time was weighed and lost: docs/decisions/ferrum-state.md, 2026-11-13.

title: `wordChars` matched by character, not by UTF-16 code unit
cm6: makeCategorizer compares each UTF-16 code unit of `wordChars` with the string (mirrors/cm6/state/src/charcategory.ts:32), so an astral entry makes every character that shares one of its surrogates a word character (fixtures/state.jsonl F0299).
better: A character is a word character when it is listed, and only then: selecting by word and word motion do not treat unrelated emoji or rare ideographs as letters.
basis: cm6's own documentation: "characters explicitly listed in the local language's wordChars" (mirrors/cm6/state/src/state.ts:369). The code-unit match is JavaScript string indexing.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to makeCategorizer that iterates code points.
note: Small and local. To check before adoption: no mirrored consumer passes an astral `wordChars` (lang-css "-", lang-javascript "$").

title: Transaction extenders contribute once when a filter returns specs
cm6: Extenders run once more for a transaction whose filter returned specs, and their effects and annotations are added again (mirrors/cm6/state/src/transaction.ts:352, :387).
better: An extension that adds an effect sees it once per transaction.
basis: None verified yet: no comment, CHANGELOG entry or test of cm6 says which is meant.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to transaction.ts, if adopted.
note: Needs a cm6-researcher reading of the CHANGELOG and of the consumers of duplicated effects before it can be called better.

title: Typed inputs cm6 accepts unchecked are validated alike
cm6: A change filter's ranges are used unsorted and unchecked; a range with `from > to` is kept; `update` with unsorted `add` fails on an empty set and passes on a non-empty one; which path reports a length mismatch between change sets varies, and operands with a zero-length unchanged section fail although their lengths agree.
better: A caller's mistake fails at the call that makes it, the same way on every path, instead of producing a state that fails later or silently.
basis: None beyond consistency; each case needs its own reading.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: Per case: a patch adding the check to cm6.
note: Risk: a check added where a consumer relies on the unchecked path (the view maps selections through replacements that give `from > to`). Each case is evaluated on the values the crates above pass.

title: `RangeSet::map` maps the ranges of a chunk a change covers
cm6: A chunk wholly covered by a change is dropped without mapping its ranges, and the drop rule of Chunk.map applies only in chunks a change touches (mirrors/cm6/state/src/rangeset.ts:151, :300-330), so whether a range survives a large replacement depends on the chunk layout.
better: Whether a decoration or marker survives an edit depends on the edit and its map mode, not on how many ranges were stored before it.
basis: None verified: the skip is an optimization of cm6 and may be intended.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to rangeset.ts, if adopted.
note: Cost: the skip is what keeps mapping a large set cheap; needs the benchmark of gate G8.

title: Range sets and cursors beyond 1,000,000,000 positions
cm6: `C.Far = 1e9` is the end sentinel and bound of range sets (mirrors/cm6/state/src/rangeset.ts:98).
better: Documents above about 954 MiB of text can carry decorations. With positions in bytes (D1) the bound is reached at fewer characters than in cm6 for non-ASCII text, which is below the floor for such a document.
basis: The goal of large documents (docs/foundation/ferrum-foundation.md §1); the bound is a JavaScript small-integer convenience.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: The sentinel is visible in cursor output, so a patch that raises `C.Far`.
note: No consumer in sight edits a document of that size; the README lists the limit meanwhile.

title: `count_column` and `find_column` are inverse at a tab followed by an extending character
cm6: The two functions step a tab followed by an extending code point or ZWJ differently (mirrors/cm6/state/src/column.ts:8-10, :28-29; fixtures/text.jsonl F0482, F0485).
better: Rectangular selection and column motion land on the same column both ways.
basis: None verified beyond the two functions being documented as counterparts.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch to column.ts; evaluated together with state.imp.001, which changes the same stepping.

title: A state whose lines hold the separator survives the JSON round trip
cm6: `toJSON` writes the document as one string and `fromJSON` splits it again, so a document built from lines that contain the separator comes back with other lines, and with a `"\r\n"` separator a shorter length (fixtures/state.jsonl F2093, F2094).
better: Saving and restoring a state gives the same document.
basis: None verified: only documents built by hand through `Text::of` are affected.
when: ferrum-state improvement delta (after the conformance verdict, before the S0 of ferrum-view)
reference: A patch, if adopted; it would change the JSON form, which cm6 clients read.
note: Changing the JSON form costs interchange with cm6; validating lines in `Text::of` costs a scan cm6 avoids.

title: Calls that take a position from outside the program can fail without a panic
cm6: cm6 throws a RangeError that a caller can catch.
better: An application that receives positions it cannot check first (a late LSP answer, a collaboration peer) handles the failure instead of crashing.
basis: D13 records this as what the panic contract gives up.
when: the specification of ferrum-view, or the first consumer that shows the need, whichever comes first
reference: Written tests; the fallible variants add to the API and displace nothing.
note: Adding them later breaks no caller (D13).

title: A document structure that keeps very long lines cheap
cm6: `Text` is a tree of lines; one line is one string, so an edit in a line of many megabytes copies it (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts).
better: Minified or generated files with enormous lines edit as fast as others.
basis: The goal of native performance; no measurement yet.
when: gate G8 of ferrum-state conformance, on a benchmark with long lines
reference: None needed if the observable behavior is unchanged; `Text::children` exposes the shape, so a change of shape is observable.
note: D2 keeps cm6's tree because nothing measured shows it missing a target.
